stories.title: Set up the TypeScript + Vite project with lint, type check and unit tests
stories.description: Create the project skeleton: package.json (exact dependency versions), package-lock.json, tsconfig.json (strict), vite.config.ts (dev server on port 5173 with strictPort), eslint.config.js (flat config with typescript-eslint), vitest.config.ts (environment 'node'; unit tests are tests/**/*.test.ts; tests/e2e/ is excluded), index.html with the title 'Spine Fluoro Trainer', and a minimal src/app/main.ts. Dependencies: typescript, vite, three, @types/three, vitest, eslint, typescript-eslint, and @playwright/test pinned to exactly 1.63.0 (used from F0-S2; do NOT run 'playwright install'). Do NOT add a browser stand-in such as jsdom or happy-dom: unit-tested logic is kept free of browser code (owner decision 2026-11-09, see docs/DECISIONS.md). npm scripts: dev, build, test (vitest run), lint (eslint + tsc --noEmit), typecheck (tsc --noEmit), and check (for now: lint, typecheck and test; F0-S2 adds screen tests). The first unit test is tests/core/project-config.test.ts: it reads package.json and index.html as text and imports vite.config.ts and vitest.config.ts, so the set-up below is checked automatically. SHARED FILES: this story creates package.json, package-lock.json, tsconfig.json, vite.config.ts, eslint.config.js, vitest.config.ts and index.html, and is explicitly allowed to. No test suite exists before this story; a failing baseline in step 3 is expected and is not a separate fix.

stories.title: Add the shared tissue labels, vertebral levels and shared types
stories.description: Create src/core/labels.ts and src/core/types.ts, the contracts every later feature builds on. labels.ts: a numbered list of tissue labels (8-bit ids, 0 = air) with a short id and a display name, containing at least: air, skin/fat (one label), muscle, cortical bone, cancellous bone, disc, ligamentum flavum, epidural space, thecal sac, spinal cord, nerve root, artery, vein and joint space; plus helpers such as isBone(label). It also lists the vertebral level codes used by the level volume (C1…C7, T1…T12, L1…L5, sacrum, ilium; 0 = no level) and sides (left/right; +x is the patient's left). types.ts: the shared types named in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Components, with only the fields the spec needs: Volume (size, voxel spacing in mm, origin/orientation, region name, 8-bit intensity, 8-bit labels, optional 8-bit levels — F1.1, F1.3, F1.6); Landmarks (region name plus one entry per vertebral level with: level code, body centre, left and right pedicle centres, superior and inferior endplate centres each with a tilt direction (unit normal vector), left and right superior articular process tips, and optional left and right foramen centres; all points in mm, patient coordinates — F1.5, F10.1, F11.2. A foramen is listed under the level above it, because in the lumbar spine that level's nerve root exits there, e.g. the L4–L5 foramen is listed under L4; this is how a nerve-contact event knows its level and side — F6.3); Mode ('practice' | 'exam' | 'quiz' | 'freeplay' — F6.1, F8.5, F10.4, F12.2); CArmPose (oblique and tilt in degrees, table left/right, head/foot and height in mm — F3.1); NeedleState (needle id, pre-bend, entry point, hub angles, bevel angle, inserted depth, shaft curve points, tip — F4, F5); TissueEvent (type: lossOfResistance, boneContact, duralPuncture, nerveContact, intravascular, cordContact, injection; time; tip position; message; optional level/side/volume/compartment — F6.2, F6.3, F9.6); AttemptRecord (kind: 'procedure' | 'quiz'; procedure id (procedure attempts only); mode; date; total score; score parts; unsafe flag, shots and fluoro time (optional, procedure attempts only) — F10.5, F11.4). Follow the coordinate and unit conventions in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Conventions (document them in comments). SHARED FILES: creates files in src/core/; explicitly allowed. Later features can only change these through an interactive session, so check every field against the spec. Before merging F0, the owner or a reviewer reads types.ts against this list.

isBone() is true for cortical and cancellous bone only

Unit test (tests/core/types.test.ts): '@ts-expect-error' lines show the type check rejects a Mode outside the four values and a TissueEvent type outside the seven listed

stories.notes: Done 2026-11-09. Choices for the owner/reviewer to check in types.ts: points are {x,y,z} objects (Vec3); level codes in Landmarks/TissueEvent are strings ('L4'), with numeric ids only in the level volume (LEVEL_IDS: C1=1 … L5=24, sacrum=25, ilium=26); table offsets: tableLeftRight along x (+ = patient's left), tableHeadFoot along z (+ = head), tableHeight along y (+ = up/posterior) — F0-S8 should follow this; NeedleState.hubAngles is {pitch, yaw} relative to the down-the-beam start direction; bevelAngle is the hub notch clock angle (0 = 12 o'clock); AttemptRecord is a union: quiz records cannot carry procedureId/shots/fluoroTimeSeconds; unsafe is on both kinds; TissueEvent.compartment uses ContrastCompartment (epidural, intrathecal, intraArticular, softTissue, intravascular).

stories.title: Add the central state store, event bus and seeded random numbers
stories.description: Create src/core/store.ts: one central store holding the shared state that crosses zones: current C-arm pose (default 0°/0° with the table at 0), shot count (0), fluoro time in seconds (0), last image pose (none until the first image), mode (default 'freeplay'), current volume (none until loaded), current landmarks (none until loaded), needle state (none = no needle), and contrast absorption volume (none = no contrast; same grid as the volume). The current region name is read from the volume, not stored twice. get, set and subscribe. Add a small typed event bus (emit/on/off) with these events: 'exposure', 'caseStart' (a new case starts; counters reset — F3.6) and 'tissueEvent' (payload: a TissueEvent — F6.3, F9.6). Create src/core/random.ts: a seeded random number generator (the same seed gives the same sequence). Plain TypeScript, no browser code. SHARED FILES: creates files in src/core/; explicitly allowed.

stories.title: Generate the synthetic phantom: layout and tissue labels
stories.description: Create src/core/phantom.ts: a function that generates a small, deterministic, labelled Volume (no larger than 128×128×128 voxels) used by all tests instead of the real CT. This story builds the labels only (intensity, levels and landmarks come in F0-S7). It contains every tissue label in src/core/labels.ts, and two vertebra-like blocks (cortical shell, cancellous inside, a disc between the bodies) with a foramen between them on each side (left and right) containing nerve root voxels, a joint space between the two blocks' posterior parts, a thecal sac with spinal cord inside, epidural space and ligamentum flavum behind it, muscle, a skin/fat layer and air around it, plus an artery and a vein. Keep a margin of air around the body so the phantom does not fill a typical C-arm field (F0-S15 needs air in the image corners). Export documented test points: the vertebra block centres, the left and right foramen centres, and a midline back-to-front test line between the two blocks' posterior parts (interlaminar). Follow docs/ARCHITECTURE.md → Conventions (+y = posterior, +x = patient's left, mm). SHARED FILES: creates a file in src/core/; explicitly allowed.

stories.title: Add C-arm projection geometry (pose to source, detector, project and unproject)
stories.description: Create src/core/geometry.ts: given a CArmPose, compute the X-ray source position, the detector plane and a 512×512 pixel grid, and provide project(point) → pixel and unproject(pixel) → ray (origin + direction). Patient prone; the isocentre is the origin of the table-relative frame; table offsets move the patient relative to the isocentre; oblique rotates about the patient's long axis (z), tilt (cranial/caudal) about the left-right axis (x). Oblique sign (owner decision 2026-11-09, see docs/DECISIONS.md): positive oblique = right, meaning the detector (above the patient's back at 0°) swings toward the patient's right side (−x) and the source toward the left; at +90° the detector is on the patient's right and the source on the patient's left. Tilt sign (owner decision 2026-11-09): positive tilt = cranial, meaning the detector tilts toward the patient's head (+z) and the source toward the feet; negative = caudal. Use typical mobile C-arm distances (owner decision 2026-11-09: typical values, no specific machine) (source-to-detector and source-to-isocentre distance, detector size) as exported, commented named constants; the tests do not depend on their exact values. Degrees in the public API, radians only inside. Document the sign conventions (oblique and tilt as above, which way is image up) in comments. Test points inside the phantom come from src/core/random.ts with a fixed seed. SHARED FILES: creates a file in src/core/; explicitly allowed.
acceptance: For at least 20 poses spread across oblique −90…+90° and tilt −40…+40°, and for table offsets of 0 and of non-zero values in all three directions, the isocentre projects to the image centre (within 0.5 px)
For seeded random points inside the phantom and at least 10 poses, projecting a point and then unprojecting the pixel gives a ray that passes within 0.1 mm of the original point

At pose (0°, 0°) the beam is a straight AP beam for a prone patient: the source is anterior (−y, under the table), the detector is posterior (+y, above the back), and the central ray is parallel to the y axis
At oblique +90° (tilt 0°) the central ray is parallel to the x axis, the detector centre has x < 0 (patient's right) and the source has x > 0 (lateral beam)
At oblique +25° (tilt 0°) the detector centre has x < 0 and y > 0; at −25° it has x > 0 and y > 0
At tilt +20° (oblique 0°) the detector centre has z > 0 and y > 0 and the source has z < 0 (cranial); at tilt −20° the detector centre has z < 0 (caudal)
Unit tests in tests/core/geometry.test.ts pass

stories.title: March X-ray rays through the phantom on the GPU and show its outline
stories.description: In the render zone, replace the flat fill with the first half of a GPU X-ray image (DRR): upload the store's volume intensity as a 3D texture (Three.js Data3DTexture), and in a fragment shader march each pixel's ray from the X-ray source to the detector using src/core/geometry.ts (same pose, same 512×512 grid). This proves the shader and geometry.ts agree before the absorption maths is added in F0-S15. Screen tests compute expected pixels by importing src/core/geometry.ts and src/core/phantom.ts in the test itself (plain TypeScript). Only the fluoro panel's rendering changes.

stories.title: Render the GPU X-ray image of the phantom with bone dark and air light
stories.description: In the render zone, replace the outline from F0-S14 with the X-ray absorption law: along each ray, add up absorption from the intensity values, and display brightness = e^(−total absorption) so that more absorption is darker (bone dark, soft tissue grey, air light). Noise, collimation, magnification, flips and the CPU reference are F2, not this story. The screen test computes the expected pixel positions by importing src/core/geometry.ts and src/core/phantom.ts in the test itself.
acceptance: Screen test (desktop, spacebar) and (tablet, tap 'Shot'): after one image at the default pose, the grey value at the projected centre of a phantom vertebra block is at least 50 lower (darker) than the grey value at an image corner (air)
